TITLE: National Youth Leadership Training (NYLT) 2027
DESC:
National Youth Leadership Training is an exciting, action-packed program designed for councils to provide youth members with leadership skills and experience they can use in their home troops and in other situations demanding leadership of self and others.  The NYLT course centers around the concepts of what a leader must BE, what a leader must KNOW, and what a leader must DO. The key elements are then taught with a clear focus on HOW TO. The skills come alive during the week as the patrol goes on a Quest for the Meaning of Leadership.

All events over 72 hours require all participants and staff to have a completed Annual Health and Medical Record (medical form) regardless of their length of participation. Click HERE to download a fillable PDF copy. Click HERE for an FAQ on the medical form.

TITLE: NOAC 2027 Registration
DESC:
Registration NOAC (National Order of the Arrow Conference) - July 26 - 31, 2027
University of Illinois Urbana-Campaign

The National Order of the Arrow Conference (NOAC) is the flagship national Order of the Arrow event. It has been three (3) years since the last NOAC held Boulder, Colorado.were a total of 7,217 Scouts and Arrowmen attended. Scouts came from all 50 states in order to participate in the NOAC.  It is second only to the BSA National Jamboree in size and scope. The largest conference was in 2015, attended by more than 15,000 Arrowmen to commemorate the 100th anniversary of the Order of the Arrow. They expect at least 8,000 Arrowmen to attend in 2027, from over 200 councils and groups. There is something for everyone whether you like training, games, patch trading or the nightly stadium shows.

This is registration. We will be traveling by bus to the University of Illinios. Buses contain 52 usable seats, we have made a decision on one bus.  If you would like a slot to go to NOAC 2027 and you do not participate in the early registration, your chances to go with the contingent will be greatly diminished.  In order to get the early registration price, full payment has to be made to NOAC, in early January.  If you do not make the deadline for full payment, you will still be able to go but will not get the discounted price.

TITLE: Cub Scout Day Camp at HMSR - Week 5
EVENT_TITLE: Cub Scout Day Camp at HMSR
DESC:
Dive Into the Adventure!

Get ready to make a splash this summer at Hawk Mountain Scout Reservation!

With five weeks of Cub Scout Day Camp to choose from, Scouts can spend their days exploring, creating, climbing, splashing, and discovering something new around every corner. From range and target sports, trolley rides, and the bouldering wall to field games, nature conservation, pool time, crafts, STEM adventures, and so much more, there’s an adventure waiting for everyone!

Build skills, work toward rank achievements, make new friends, and create memories that will last a lifetime. Whether you join us for one week or dive into several, we can’t wait to see you at camp!

 

Sessions:

Session 1: June 21st-June 25th

Session 2: June 28th-July 2nd

Session 3: July 5th-July 9th

Session 4: July 12th-July 16th

Session 5: July 19th-July 23rd

 

Parts A and B of Scouting America's Annual Health and Medical Record (medical form) is needed for all participants.

TITLE: Scouts BSA Summer Camp 2027 - Week 5
DESC:
Register for Summer Camp 2027 at Hawk Mountain Scout Reservation!

A $20 per person deposit is required to reserve your unit’s campsite and week at Hawk Mountain Scout Reservation. The deposit will be applied toward your unit’s overall summer camp balance. The number of participants may be adjusted at a later date, allowing units to add or remove participants as needed.

Adult Attendance Discounts
In an effort to help ensure Safeguarding Youth policies are followed, 2 free leaders per unit, no minimum youth count! Additional free leader discounts starts at 10 youth. Units bringing 11-15 youth receive 1 additional free adult registration, and units bringing 16+ receive another free adult registration.

Our premier Scouts BSA camp offers a variety of programs, including First Year Camper programs, Aquatics at both our pool and lakefront, Range and Target activities, Outdoor Skills, Nature, Handicraft, Climbing, Zip-lining, and more.

Family Night BBQ Chicken Dinners can be purchased on each registration slot. More details to come soon!

Merit Badge Offerings
While we don't have anything set in stone yet, you will be able to check out the schedule and catalog using the links on the side. Scouts are invited to sign up for their classes as soon as 50% of their camp registration cost is paid.

More details are being added regularly.

Parts A, B, and C of Scouting America's Annual Health and Medical Record (medical form) is needed for all participants.
Click HERE for more information and to download a copy from the National website on this topic.

This means that parents / guardians can edit their Scout's information or even make payments directly! Check out the Unit Leader's Guide for granting them access and then be sure to share the Parent / Guardian video with them!

TITLE: NRA Shotgun Instructor Course with BIT
EVENT_TITLE: NRA Shotgun Instructor Course with BIT
DESC:
This course with start with a 6-hour classroom course (BIT), which covers the fundamentals of teaching followed by an 11-hour course which teaches the knowledge, skills and attitude essential to organizing, promoting and teaching NRA’s Basic Shotgun Shooting course.

Prerequisite Training: NRA Basic Shotgun: You must complete these classroom courses first. You may not attend this course without NRA Basic Shotgun.

This course is intentionally offered under market rate with the understanding that attendees will sign an agreement to assist with a set number of Hawk Mountain Council Range & Target Activities during the certification period.

This course will start promptly at 8:00 AM, Lunch is provided on Saturday ending on Sunday at 1pm.

NRA Instructor Courses Require 4 participants to run the class. You will be notified with options, if there are not enough participants.

As with all Scouting events, participants must have a completed Annual Health & Medical Record. Only parts A and B are required for events under 72 hours. Click HERE to download a copy.

TITLE: Orienteering Merit Badge Weekend
DESC:
Orienteering Adventure Weekend!

Get ready to put your navigation skills to the test! Join us for a full weekend of hands-on orienteering, led by experienced professionals and featuring a mix of classroom instruction and real-world field exercises.

Scouts who complete the weekend will:

  • Earn the Orienteering Merit Badge
  • Build practical map, compass, and navigation skills
  • Put those skills into action in the field
  • Receive FREE admission to the corresponding DVOA orienteering event on Sunday
  • Enjoy all meals included throughout the weekend - Cracker Barrel Friday, 3 hot meals and Cracker Barrel Saturday, continental breakfast and trail lunch Sunday

Whether you’re brand new to orienteering or ready to sharpen your skills, this will be a weekend of learning, adventure, and putting your abilities to the test.

$50 if signed up by March 1st - secure your spot with a $10 deposit today!

As with all Scouting America events and activities, Parts A and B of Scouting America's Annual Health and Medical Record (medical form) is needed for all participants.
Click HERE for more information and to download a copy from the National website on this topic.

TITLE: 2027 Scouts BSA Klondike Derby
DESC:
2027 Klondike Derby

Bundle up, load your sled, and get ready for a day of winter adventure at the Klondike Derby!

Put your patrol's teamwork, leadership, and Scouting skills to the test as you navigate a series of exciting challenges!

Scouts will work together to pull their sleds from station to station, tackling challenges that test their knowledge, problem-solving abilities, and ability to work as a team. From first aid and fire building to knots, navigation, cooking, and more, each station offers an opportunity to put Scouting skills into action - all while having fun!

Event Details:

  • Saturday, January 16, 2027
  • 8:00 AM – 4:00 PM
  • $15 per participant
  • Scouts BSA Troops, Venturing Crews, and Sea Scout Ships welcomed!
  • All Scouts will receive a special event patch!

What to Expect:

  • Patrol-based challenges and friendly competition
  • Hands-on Scouting skills and winter activities
  • Teamwork, leadership, and problem-solving opportunities
  • A full day of outdoor adventure, regardless of what winter weather brings!

Station Listing:

  • First Aid
  • Cooking
  • Knots
  • Inspection
  • Shooting Sports
  • Compass
  • Firebuilding
  • Surprise
  • Totin' Chio
  • Gear Room
  • ice Rescue (simulated)

TITLE: Scouts BSA Winter STEM Camp
DESC:
Looking for an adventure over winter break? Join us at Hawk Mountain Scout Reservation for STEM Winter Camp, four days of science, technology, discovery, and fun!

Scouts will explore the exciting world of STEM through hands-on activities, interactive challenges, and opportunities to work toward four merit badges:

  • Nuclear Science – Explore the fascinating world of atoms, radiation, and nuclear energy.
  • Robotics – Discover engineering and programming through hands-on robotics challenges.
  • Astronomy – Explore the universe, stars, and constellations, including experiences in our indoor star dome.
  • Competitive Gaming NEW – Put your strategy, teamwork, and sportsmanship to the test!

But the adventure doesn't stop with merit badges! Scouts will also enjoy:

  • Skills for Life workshops, including Financial Literacy 101
  • First Aid and CPR certification opportunities
  • STEM-themed evening programs
  • Gaming tournaments and a closing-night celebration
  • Movie that ties to the theme, games, and time to make new friends

With small instructional groups, Scouts will have opportunities to learn by doing, try something new, and develop skills they can use beyond Scouting.

Registration includes: Three nights of lodging, meals throughout camp, program materials, and an exclusive Winter Camp patch!

Cost: $325 per Scout

Space is limited, so don't wait to register!

As with all Scouting events, participants must have a completed Annual Health & Medical Record. Only parts A and B are required for events under 72 hours. Click HERE to download a copy.

Merit badge completion depends on individual requirements, participation, and any necessary prerequisites. Additional details will be provided before camp.

TITLE: OA Lodge Leadership Development (LLD)
DESC:
LLD (Lodge Leadership Development)

Lodge Leadership Development is the primary training program for local lodges, providing lodge leadership with the skills needed to plan and run a successful lodge program. The LLD program is designed to equip lodges with the tools to stimulate creative ideas and develop lasting solutions that will enable and enhance growth.

We will be hosting an all-day training session. Attendees should bring their own lunch. If you have dietary restrictions, please indicate them during registration. Also, please bring clothing for outdoor activities.

There is no cost for this event. This is a training event, and we want to encourage all youth and adults in the lodge to attend this fantastic training and growth opportunity.

What to Bring

Scouts will need to bring a copy of the BSA Annual Medical and Health Review (AMHR) Parts A&B with them to the event.

Scouts should bring a small notebook and writing instrument for notes. All other materials will be provided.

Scouts can optionally bring a water bottle, but juice/soda/water and other light refreshments will be made available.

Schedule

9:00am: Arrival and Registration

9:30am- 12:00pm: Morning sessions

12:00-1:00pm: Lunch and photos

1:00-4:00pm: Afternoon sessions

4:00pm: Leave for home

DESC:
Order of the Arrow dues are now being collected for the 2026 calendar year.  Dues are $20.00 per member.

DESC:
This course teaches the basic knowledge, skills, and attitude necessary for the safe use of a shotgun in target shooting. Students learn NRA’s rules for safe firearm handling, shotgun parts and operation, ammunition, shooting fundamentals, range rules, cleaning, and continued opportunities for skill development.
This is for the NRA Basic Shotgun course - this is not an instructor course.

This course is required before taking BIT and the NRA Shotgun Instructor courses.

This a full, action-packed course that will start Friday promptly at 6pm - Saturday morning at 8am - 12pm

TITLE: 2026 OA Brotherhood Service Day - Kittatinny Brotherhood Day
DESC:
We will be having a single day of service followed by a Brotherhood Ceremony for our fellow Arrowman sealing their bonds.

Schedule

Registration starts at 8:30am. Service starts at 9:00am. We will break for lunch, and then service from 12:30-2:00pm. Brotherhood ceremony will start at 2:30pm, followed by a short cracker barrel and our November Lodge Executive Committee Meeting. We are encouraging all registered members of the lodge, youth and adult, to attend this day of cheerful service. Departure will be around 4:00pm.

What to Bring

Attendees should bring their own water bottle, work clothes/gloves, and uniform for ceremonies. Lunch and cracker barrel will be provided.

Scouts will need to bring a copy of the BSA Annual Medical and Health Review (AMHR) Parts A&B with them to the event.

Special Notes

  • All Ordeal members who took their Ordeal during or before the May 2026 service weekend (including previous years) are eligible and encouraged to take their Brotherhood at this event.
  • Ordeal members who took their Ordeal at September 2026 weekend are encouraged to attend the event and cracker barrel, but will not be able to attend the ceremony. We will have other activities for these Arrowmen while the ceremony is occurring. We invite you to come back to take your Brotherhood in the spring of 2027.

TITLE: NRA Basic Instructor Training (BIT)
DESC:
NRA Basic Instructor Training equips participants with the knowledge, skills, and attitude to conduct NRA Basic Firearm courses and become certified instructors.

NRA Basic Instructor Training is a mandatory pre-requisite for all NRA instructor-level courses. It is designed for individuals who already have basic firearm safety and shooting skills and want to teach NRA courses effectively. The course focuses on policies, procedures, and teaching methods necessary to conduct NRA Basic Firearm Training Courses, ensuring students earn recognized NRA certification.

You must complete this 6-hour classroom course, which covers the fundamentals of teaching, within the two years prior to individual discipline instructor training.

As with all Scouting events, participants must have a completed Annual Health & Medical Record. Only parts A and B are required for events under 72 hours. Click HERE to download a copy.

TITLE: NRA Range Safety Officer (RSO) Course
DESC:
The NRA Range Safety Officer program provides nationally recognized certification for individuals responsible for supervising safe shooting activities and range operations.

The Range and Target requirement to run a rifle range on scouting property is 1 NRA RSO and 1 NRA Rifle Instructor.

This will be an action packed course that will start promptly at 8:00 am and finish at 6:00 pm, lunch will be included.

This course is intentionally offered under market rate with the understanding that attendees will sign an agreement to assist with a set number of Hawk Mountain Council Range & Target Activities during the certification period.

After this course, you will be able to:

  • Supervise Live Fire: Provide direct safety supervision for live-fire range events involving Scouts BSA, Venturing, and Sea Scouts.

  • Enforce Safety Rules: Manage range commands, monitor shooter behavior, and ensure adherence to range Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).

  • Inspect Ranges: Conduct pre-activity range inspections and verify proper equipment and environmental setups.

  • Handle Emergencies: Manage range emergencies, medical protocols, and firearm stoppages or malfunctions.
     

As with all Scouting events, participants must have a completed Annual Health & Medical Record. Only parts A and B are required for events under 72 hours. Click HERE to download a copy.

TITLE: Frontier First Aid Meet
DESC:
This event is an opportunity for a patrol of 4 - 6 scouts or venturers to put their first aid skills and knowledge to the test by completing 4 - 6 first aid scenarios in competition with other patrols. The top 5 patrols from the basic scenarios will then go on to complete in a more challenging scenario to determine the top 5 place winner order.

Each unit participating must nominate at least one adult to serve as a judge. Arrow of Light Cub Scouts are welcome to attend as scenario victims with their associated troop.
